tool.summary: The MMD permutation null shuffles labels within a subject. The primary and control comparisons are paired by sample, and every subject carries four very different poses, so the shuffle mixes poses and the null comes out far wider than the design's. The MMD q is then nearly always >= 0.05, so the MMD can never veto, and 'undecided' turns into 'matched' or 'indistinguishable'. The PREREG froze this null ('shuffled within each subject both sets hold'), so the code is faithful to a wrong frozen rule.
tool.scenario: Kept edits against FluXray. Each of the 100 subjects has 4 drawn poses (different heights, offsets and rotations, so different anatomy), and each sample has 2 edits plus 1 FluXray image. The observed sets are pose-balanced per sample. A permutation by strata() moves FluXray labels across poses inside the subject, so the permuted label-1 set gets a different pose mix and the permuted MMD goes up. I ran the real mmd_test and c2st on synthetic features shaped like this (pose spread 3, subject 1, noise 1; scratch script review-scratch/perm_sim.py). Under an exact null, the within-subject p was 1.0 in 6 of 6 repetitions; shuffling within sample gave p spread from 0.015 to 0.94. With a real edit shift of 0.15, the code's p was 0.72 to 0.95 against 0.005 within sample, and the c2st AUC was about 0.51 with lower bound about 0.49. So in every space the verdict is matched or indistinguishable when it should be undecided, and replication_word returns 'reproduced' for edits that differ from FluXray. With a weaker pose effect (spread 1) the null p was still 0.62 to 1.0. The same null drives the per-arm words. No test checks the paired-design null: test_a_pair_of_sets_of_the_same_cts_reads_as_chance_and_not_below_it only asserts p > 0.05, which an overly conservative null passes, and the MMD tests use disjoint subjects.
